# Values

## User understandable over technical language

I feel like code should always be understandable by users as they are the ones who dictate process. So the goal of code should make it the most understandable with zero context as possible

### Principles

- Long variables names where needed to be descriptive
- Avoid using technical language such as “factory” or “barrel”
- Stick to a common language profile, (tasks always being tasks, stages always being stages etc)
- File structure should reflect the call stack
- Use of JSDocs to explain variables in pure english
- Include why things are done not just what is done
- Use a labelled data inport pattern (IE  `({varA , varB}) => {}`)
- NEVER MENTION DESIGN PATTERNS
- Use @example tags in js doc to easily explain functionality
- Every new export also carries a `MARK:` label in the same JSDoc block, sitting directly above the export (only whitespace between `*/` and `export`); `npm run check:jsdoc-example` (<1s) checks this before pushing — copy-paste shapes in docs/agent-docs/KB-Code-Standards.md §Documentation/Jsdoc
  
  

## Functional over Object oreintated

Although pure functional code can tend to insanity it is always important to note co-mingle state and functionality. Where possible state should leave in clearly defined places, and functions should show a clear line in how we move from one state to another. Traditional object oriented design mainly serves to gatekeep devs(or for game dev).

### Principles

- Try and avoid using classes where possible
- Currying can be used to create sudo classes, avoid that
- Functions should follow black box mentality, clear input delivers the same output with no side affects
- Treat variables as immutable unless they are clearly defined states.
- Functions should always be named with a verb in, as they are doing something
- Give the miniumn data to each function as possible. Pick off fields before invocation.
- Each function should only work to achieve its task, with a single responsibility


## Co-location over abstraction

Although abstraction is an essential part of coding it should always only be done by business level intent, not just on functionality. Ideally if you pick a random file in the codebase you should only need to look at the one folder above it and one folder under it to get all the context on its functionality.

### Principles
- Unit tests should always be placed next to the relevant file
- Generally functions called in a higher function should be placed in a folder of that functions name. IE if `funA.js` calls `funB.js` it should be `./funA/funB.js`
- Generic/helper functions should only be made if they are repeatedly doing the same thing.
- Helpers should be treated like react state and exist at the lowest level folder that is common in the hierarchy of the folders
- If abstracting it would take up more lines/characters than just embedding that line directly on a per file basis avoid doing it. IE don’t abstract a single line just because its repeated unless it has some complex logic like a regex.
- Don’t fear repetition of code
- Make sure the code is easily searchable for any given task. If I said modify the task history box in the ui it should  be easy and logical to figure out where that is.
- Use folders as a tool for organising

## Tested over trusted 

Functionality should not assumed to exist until it is tested and evidenced. “it should work” isn’t always reliable and we want to make sure there are no regressions. 

### Principles
- Try and at least plan what tests you are going to make before you  code a function
- Don’t assume typing is correct until proven, or allow it to fail safe
- Failures should clear transparent and observable, every function doesnt need to intensly check it just needs to report failures accurately
- Tests must be consistent
- Integration test must reflect how a user could want to use the app
- Use the lowest possible level of tests( Ie Unit over api over e2e) for the fastest test cycle


## Fast iteration over long planning

Sometimes you just can’t know what will happen without using it and that is essential. Spending too long planning can cause ideas to get confused or get you trapped in a loop where you just make plans worse.  Having simple clear checkpoints is great.

### Principles
- When planning, factor in points to check certain things and how the plan can be adapted when needed
- Try and create safe ways to test functionality, ie not in prod, when possible as this will allow you to confirm things work.
- Focus on one small change at a time, get tests passing then work on the next element.
- Always design code with the intent it will be changed/replaced soon
- Minimise friction in development even if it is small
- Make change easy, then make the change. Even if making change easy is hard.



# Inspirations
My principles here are inspired by:

- Extreme programming Explained by Kent Beck (book)
- Life isn’t binary (book)
- Intent driven design by David whitney (Talk)


# Examples

## Intent Driven descriptions

### Bad Example

```js

const userInOneYearFactory = (name, age, users) => {

    const user = {name: name , age: age + 1}

    users.push(user)
  
}

const list = []

userFactory("Frank",32,list)


```

## Good example

```js

/**
* MARK: calculateAgeNextYear
* @description calculates the age someone will be next year
* @example const usersAgeNextYear = calculateAgeNextYear({ageNow: 3})  
console.log(usersAgeNextYear) // 4
*/
const calculateAgeNextYear = ({ageNow}) => {
  const ageNextYear = ageNow + 1

# Values

## User understandable over technical language

I feel like code should always be understandable by users as they are the ones who dictate process. So the goal of code should make it the most understandable with zero context as possible

### Principles

- Long variables names where needed to be descriptive
- Avoid using technical language such as “factory” or “barrel”
- Stick to a common language profile, (tasks always being tasks, stages always being stages etc)
- File structure should reflect the call stack
- Use of JSDocs to explain variables in pure english
- Include why things are done not just what is done
- Use a labelled data inport pattern (IE  `({varA , varB}) => {}`)
- NEVER MENTION DESIGN PATTERNS
- Use @example tags in js doc to easily explain functionality
- Every new export also carries a `MARK:` label in the same JSDoc block, sitting directly above the export (only whitespace between `*/` and `export`); `npm run check:jsdoc-example` (<1s) checks this before pushing — copy-paste shapes in docs/agent-docs/KB-Code-Standards.md §Documentation/Jsdoc
  
  

## Functional over Object oreintated

Although pure functional code can tend to insanity it is always important to note co-mingle state and functionality. Where possible state should leave in clearly defined places, and functions should show a clear line in how we move from one state to another. Traditional object oriented design mainly serves to gatekeep devs(or for game dev).

### Principles

- Try and avoid using classes where possible
- Currying can be used to create sudo classes, avoid that
- Functions should follow black box mentality, clear input delivers the same output with no side affects
- Treat variables as immutable unless they are clearly defined states.
- Functions should always be named with a verb in, as they are doing something
- Give the miniumn data to each function as possible. Pick off fields before invocation.
- Each function should only work to achieve its task, with a single responsibility


## Co-location over abstraction

Although abstraction is an essential part of coding it should always only be done by business level intent, not just on functionality. Ideally if you pick a random file in the codebase you should only need to look at the one folder above it and one folder under it to get all the context on its functionality.

### Principles
- Unit tests should always be placed next to the relevant file
- Generally functions called in a higher function should be placed in a folder of that functions name. IE if `funA.js` calls `funB.js` it should be `./funA/funB.js`
- Generic/helper functions should only be made if they are repeatedly doing the same thing.
- Helpers should be treated like react state and exist at the lowest level folder that is common in the hierarchy of the folders
- If abstracting it would take up more lines/characters than just embedding that line directly on a per file basis avoid doing it. IE don’t abstract a single line just because its repeated unless it has some complex logic like a regex.
- Don’t fear repetition of code
- Make sure the code is easily searchable for any given task. If I said modify the task history box in the ui it should  be easy and logical to figure out where that is.
- Use folders as a tool for organising

## Tested over trusted 

Functionality should not assumed to exist until it is tested and evidenced. “it should work” isn’t always reliable and we want to make sure there are no regressions. 

### Principles
- Try and at least plan what tests you are going to make before you  code a function
- Don’t assume typing is correct until proven, or allow it to fail safe
- Failures should clear transparent and observable, every function doesnt need to intensly check it just needs to report failures accurately
- Tests must be consistent
- Integration test must reflect how a user could want to use the app
- Use the lowest possible level of tests( Ie Unit over api over e2e) for the fastest test cycle


## Fast iteration over long planning

Sometimes you just can’t know what will happen without using it and that is essential. Spending too long planning can cause ideas to get confused or get you trapped in a loop where you just make plans worse.  Having simple clear checkpoints is great.

1|# Design note — collapsed alias-row layout (Step 0)
2|
3|Decision for the alias-screen redo (issue: model names cut off mid-name in the
4|collapsed summary, `assets/image.png`). Survey round-1 answers are still empty,
5|so the proposed defaults in `IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` §1 bind: q1 whole alias
6|screen, q2 wrap-before-ellipsis, q3 provider as a badge, q4 mobile gets its own
7|full-width line, q5 compact rows by default, q6 error badge on its own line.
8|
9|## Before (current markup, `ModelAliasesSection.jsx` ~:1238)
10|
11|```
12|┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
13|│ ▸ name │ summary-badge (one hard-truncated line) │ ⚠err │ rel │ ✕ │  ← one flex line, everything competes
14|└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
15|section root capped at max-w-2xl (672px) even on a 1440px+ desktop page
16|```
17|
18|`TruncatedText` applies `truncate` (one-line ellipsis), so a long
19|`provider::model` ref — exactly what the summary badge holds — is cut mid-name.
20|
21|## After (chosen layout)
22|
23|```
24|┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
25|│ ▸ name  reliability-line                              ✕        │  ← header line
26|│ ┌────────────────────────────┐ ┌────────────────────────────┐ │  ← line 2: full-width wrapping chips
27|│ │ 50% Muse [google] gemini-… │ │ 50% pi [anthropic] claude-…│ │    (data-testid=model-alias-summary-{i})
28|│ └────────────────────────────┘ └────────────────────────────┘ │
29|│ [⚠ error badge — own full-width line when present]            │
30|└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
31|section root spans the FULL width of the settings panel (no max-w cap) — this section only
32|```
33|
34|## Decisions
35|
36|- **(a) Two-line collapsed row.** Line 1 = toggle + alias name (still
37|  `truncate` — names are short by design) + reliability + delete. Line 2 =
38|  `w-full flex flex-wrap gap-1.5` chips container carrying
39|  `data-testid="model-alias-summary-{i}"` (existing test id survives on the
40|  container). On `<sm` the flex-wrap structure makes line 2 naturally
41|  full-width under the header (q4 option 1) — verified at 390px.
42|- **(b) Chip structure.** `percent` (bold, nowrap) + harness label (nowrap) +
43|  provider badge (small uppercase) + model id (`font-mono`, `min-w-0 flex-1`,
44|  `break-all` so it wraps before any ellipsis). Chip itself is
45|  `inline-flex flex-wrap` with `min-w-0`, so a 140+ char id wraps inside the
46|  chip instead of overflowing. Full stored ref (`harness::provider::id[::lvl]`)
47|  rides in the chip's `title` **and** an sr-only span inside the chip, so the
48|  complete ref is always in the DOM/accessibility tree (WCAG — hover alone is
49|  not enough).
50|- **(c) Truncation order.** chip wraps to next line → model id wraps
51|  (`break-all`) → single-line ellipsis only as last resort on the alias *name*
52|  (unchanged). Model refs are never ellipsized.
53|- **(d) Container width.** `max-w-2xl` → **no width cap at all** (`w-full
54|  min-w-0`) on the alias section root only, so the section uses the full width
55|  of the settings panel on desktop. Human review correction (final review
56|  2026-11-20): an intermediate `max-w-4xl` (896px) still wasted most of a
57|  1440px+ page — "make the most of the full width" means uncapped. Other
58|  settings tabs keep their `max-w-*` — intentional, noted in PR.
59|- **(e) Mobile.** No separate breakpoint needed: chips line is a full-width
60|  block under the header at every width; at 390px each chip takes the full row.
61|- **Provider split semantics** (`splitModelRefProvider`): strip optional
62|  `::reasoning` via `splitReasoning`, then split the base on the first `::`:
63|  - `google::gemini-3-pro` → `{ provider: 'google', modelId: 'gemini-3-pro' }`
64|  - `pi::google::m` (canonical 3-segment) → `{ provider: 'google', modelId: 'm' }`
65|    (the harness half is already shown by the harness label chip — not repeated)
66|  - bare `m` → `{ provider: '', modelId: 'm' }` (no badge rendered)
67|  - garbage/blank → `{ provider: '', modelId: ref }` (never throws)
68|
69|## Mock verification (scratchpad `design-spike/mock.html`, headless chromium)
70|
71|- 1440px: section spans the full panel width (no `max-w-*` on the root —
72|  verified `className` carries `w-full` and no `max-w-` class); all three
73|  chips (incl. a 204-char model id) render with `scrollWidth == clientWidth`
74|  — zero clipping; no horizontal page scroll.
75|- 390px: chips drop to full-width rows under the header; 204-char model id
76|  wraps inside its chip, fully contained, no page scroll.
77|
78|Gate: this note written; no source changes in Step 0.

1|# Implementation plan — Redo the Model Aliases screen so model names stop being cut off
2|
3|## 0. Goal
4|
5|The collapsed alias rows in Settings › Project Settings › Model Aliases truncate the model
6|summary to the point it is meaningless (screenshot: `assets/image.png`), even on desktop where
7|the rest of the page is empty. Model names carry provider prefixes (`google::gemini-3-pro`),
8|so a mid-name ellipsis destroys the information.
9|
10|Redo the alias UI so the full model reference is readable on desktop and mobile, while keeping
11|every existing behaviour intact: collapse/expand, weighted targets, validation errors, reliability
12|lines, delete, add, save/discard.
13|
14|In scope: the alias screen only — `frontend/src/components/settings/ModelAliasesSection.jsx`
15|(collapsed rows + expanded alias cards). Out of scope: the model picker on stage cards, any
16|backend/API change (none needed — this is a pure frontend layout/content change).
17|
18|Source request: task title + `assets/image.png`. Decision checklist: `SURVEY.md` (round 1,
19|questions q1–q6; answers not collected yet — see §1).
20|
21|## 1. Survey decision map (SURVEY.md round 1 — proposed defaults)
22|
23|The survey answers are still empty (`"answers": {}`), so each question gets a **proposed
24|default** derived from the issue text. Once answers land they are binding; if an answer
25|contradicts a default, only Step 0 (design spike) is revisited — Steps 1–4 are written to be
26|layout-agnostic.
27|
28|| # | Question | Proposed default (to bind when answered) |
29||---|---|---|
30|| q1 | Scope of the redo | The whole alias screen: collapsed summary rows **and** the expanded alias cards' headers. Not the stage-card model picker. |
31|| q2 | Overflow behaviour | Summary becomes its own wrapping area: model name gets the flexible width, wraps (`break-all`) before any ellipsis; small badges (reliability, warnings) sit on the first line with the name and never squeeze the model text. Ellipsis is the last resort, with the full ref always in `title` + the DOM. |
32|| q3 | Provider prefix | Model id renders as the main text with the provider as a small separate badge next to it (`google` badge + `gemini-3-pro`); the complete stored ref is never shortened in the DOM/accessibility tree — it stays in `title` and an sr-only span. |
33|| q4 | Mobile (narrow screen) | The model summary gets its own full-width line under the alias name (option 1), not a cut single line. |
34|| q5 | Many aliases | Keep compact collapsed rows by default (option 1) — one header line + one summary line per alias — full details on expand. No hover auto-expand. |
35|| q6 | Other pain points | Error/warning badges move to their own full-width line when present so they are never squeezed out; reliability line stays compact on the header line; percent split stays inside the expanded card. |
36|
37|## 2. Current-state map (verified in repo)
38|
39|Root causes of the cut-off names:
40|
41|1. **The section is width-capped.** `ModelAliasesSection.jsx:1148` renders
42|   `<div data-testid="model-aliases-section" className="space-y-3 max-w-2xl">` — 42rem (672px)
43|   max, while the settings page is much wider on desktop. This alone wastes the "rest of the
44|   page" the issue mentions. (Other settings tabs also use `max-w-2xl`, e.g.
45|   `ProjectSettings.jsx:259` — widening those is out of scope.)
46|2. **The collapsed row is one crowded flex line.** `ModelAliasesSection.jsx:1238` —
47|   `flex items-center justify-between gap-2 flex-wrap min-w-0` holds, in one row: the collapse
48|   toggle, the alias name (`truncate`, :1249), the summary badge (:1255–1260), the error badge
49|   (:1261+), the reliability line (:1283+), and the delete button (:1301+). Everything competes
50|   for the same width.
51|3. **The summary is a single hard-truncated string.** The badge wraps
52|   `<TruncatedText text={formatAliasSummary(targets, targetHarnesses)} />` (:1258).
53|   `TruncatedText` (`frontend/src/components/common/TruncatedText.jsx`) applies
54|   `min-w-0 max-w-full truncate inline-block` — a one-line ellipsis whose only full-text carrier
55|   is the hover `title`. `formatAliasSummary` (:854–880) builds one long string
56|   `"2 targets · 50% Muse (google::gemini-3-pro), 50% pi (…)"`, so a long provider-prefixed ref
57|   is exactly what gets cut.
58|4. **Model refs embed the provider.** Grammar in `shared/modelKeys.js` /
59|   `frontend/src/services/modelKeys.js`: canonical `harness::provider::id::reasoning`, legacy
60|   `provider::id`; `splitReasoning` (`shared/modelKeys.js:148`) splits the optional `::level`.
61|
62|Key files and contracts:
63|
64|| File | Role | Notes |
65||---|---|---|
66|| `frontend/src/components/settings/ModelAliasesSection.jsx` (1489 LOC) | The alias screen | MARK-documented sections: `formatAliasSummary` :854, `CollapseToggleButton` :882, `DeleteAliasButton` :914, `AliasTargetRow` :462, collapsed/expanded render :1238–1450 |
67|| `frontend/src/components/common/TruncatedText.jsx` + `.test.jsx` | Shared one-line truncation label | Used by all settings cards; keep unchanged for other cards |
68|| `frontend/src/components/settings/ReliabilityLine.jsx` | Per-alias / per-target reliability line | Rendered in the collapsed row today |
69|| `frontend/src/components/settings/useCollapsibleRows.js` + `.test.jsx` | Collapse state keyed by stable row keys | Not touched by this redo |
70|| `frontend/src/components/settings/ProjectSettingsForm.jsx:685–700` | Mount point (`activeFormSection === 'aliases'`) | Passes aliases/harnesses/fleetCounts/projectId |
71|| `ModelAliasesSection.test.jsx` (1549 LOC), `ModelAliasesSection.reliability.test.jsx` (587) | Existing component tests | Assert summary text via `model-alias-summary-{i}` (:865, :1093) |
72|| `SettingsCards.overflow.test.jsx:193–210` | Overflow contract test | Asserts the *current* "summary truncates long model refs" contract — deliberately updated in Step 5 |
73|| `TruncatedText.test.jsx`, `useCollapsibleRows.test.jsx` | Shared hook/label tests | Should stay green untouched |
74|
75|Stable test ids to preserve on the new markup: `model-aliases-section`, `model-alias-row`,
76|`model-alias-toggle-{i}`, `model-alias-summary-{i}`, `model-alias-error-alert-{i}` /
77|`model-alias-error-badge-{i}`, `alias-reliability-{i}`, `model-alias-body-{i}`.
78|
79|Repo rules that shape the implementation:
80|
81|- New files under `frontend/src/` are gated by `scripts/check-one-function-per-file.mjs`
82|  (one top-level function per new file) — so new pieces are **new files**, not more functions
83|  inside `ModelAliasesSection.jsx`.
84|- Every new/renamed export needs a `MARK:` + `@description` + runnable `@example` JSDoc block;
85|  gate: `npm run check:jsdoc-example` (see `docs/agent-docs/KB-Code-Standards.md` §Jsdoc).
86|- `npm run check:deps:frontend` guards declared imports.
87|- Accessibility: repo aligns to WCAG 2.2 AAA (`docs/accessibility/`); full model refs must stay
88|  in the DOM/accessibility tree — a hover tooltip alone is not enough.
89|
90|## 3. Approach — make the change easy, then make the change
91|
92|1. **Design spike first (Step 0)** — the only real unknown is the exact collapsed-row layout
93|   and truncation order. Settle it on a static mock before touching source.
94|2. **Make the change easy (Step 1)** — extract pure helpers + a presentational collapsed-row
95|   component into their own one-function-per-file modules with unit tests, while the current
96|   UI stays byte-identical and green. After this step the redo is prop-drilling, not surgery.
97|3. **Make the change (Steps 2–4)** — widen the container, swap the collapsed row to the new
98|   layout, polish the expanded header/error badge.

site-docs/agent-execution.md:31:Stages can run through a model alias (`harness: "alias"` + `model: "<name>"`), which resolves to one weighted harness + model target per run. The monitor always shows halves from **one** target: a live session's actuals win over the peeked rotation preview (idle/queued runs show the full peeked preview), so a run never displays an impossible combination like a `muse` harness with a Gemini model. Some harnesses (`muse`, `custom`) manage their own model (`modelSelection: "none"`): dispatch never attempts a model switch there — a requested model is ignored with a run-log note naming the alias — the monitor shows the Harness pill with no Model pill, and alias targets for those harnesses must leave the model blank (the API refuses `none` + model rows with a 400 naming the alias). Rows saved before that refusal blank the model on load with a warning.
site-docs/agent-execution.md:47:## Model alias reliability
site-docs/agent-execution.md:49:Project Settings › Aliases › Model Aliases displays per-target reliability lines under each alias target row: all-time success rate plus counted runs. Clean runs count as successes, while non-chosen failures — tool-failure loop-guard trips, connectivity errors, timeouts, and model/session errors (`failureKind: "infrastructure"`) — count as failures. As with harness reliability, **deliberate agent decisions to fail a stage are excluded** from both numerator and denominator. The settings line shows both the all-time and the recent 10-run figures (Labels: "All-time" and "Last 10 runs"); the same window is available per target to API consumers.
site-docs/submit-track-task.md:39:- The same meta line carries a small **stage model attribution** footnote (`harness · model`, plus `· alias <name>` when a model alias resolved the pick) on a row for any agent run **of that row's own stage** — the same resolved choice the session init line and the stage report's **Model** line recorded, so a model that keeps failing on one stage is easy to spot. Rows of stages that do not run an agent (CI, merge, deploy, and human checkpoints) intentionally show nothing at all — an agent run's badge never lands on another stage's row. Entries recorded before attribution existed render unchanged.

The monitor always shows halves from **one** target: a live session's actuals win over the peeked rotation preview (idle/queued runs show the full peeked preview), so a run never displays an impossible combination like a `muse` harness with a Gemini model. Some harnesses (`muse`, `custom`) manage their own model (`modelSelection: "none"`): dispatch never attempts a model switch there — a requested model is ignored with a run-log note naming the alias — the monitor shows the Harness pill with no Model pill, and alias targets for those harnesses must leave the model blank (the API refuses `none` + model rows with a 400 naming the alias). site-docs/agent-execution.md:47:## Model alias reliability
site-docs/agent-execution.md:49:Project Settings › Aliases › Model Aliases displays per-target reliability lines under each alias target row: all-time success rate plus counted runs. Clean runs count as successes, while non-chosen failures — tool-failure loop-guard trips, connectivity errors, timeouts, and model/session errors (`failureKind: "infrastructure"`) — count as failures. As with harness reliability, **deliberate agent decisions to fail a stage are excluded** from both numerator and denominator. The settings line shows both the all-time and the recent 10-run figures (Labels: "All-time" and "Last 10 runs"); the same window is available per target to API consumers.

✓ All referenced file paths exist (75 doc files scanned).

===CHANGELOG===
# Changelog

All notable changes to KainBain are recorded here in **curated** form. The
per-commit baked history that backs the in-app **Changelog** dialog is generated
by `scripts/generate-changelog.mjs` and served through `GET /deploy/changelog`
(`frontend/src/components/layout/ChangelogModal.jsx`); it remains the exhaustive
source of truth. This file intentionally lists only high-impact changes.

## Update discipline

- Entries are curated **only at release time**, from the `Unreleased` section
  below, when a version tag/deploy is cut. Ordinary PRs are not required to touch
  this file (WP-10, task `8e61e197-cf8a-475e-b330-8cd7fa5a7e30`).
- Keep entries to one line each, grouped under `Added` / `Changed` / `Fixed` /
  `Removed` / `Security`. Reference the PR or task id in parentheses when
  helpful. Do not copy auto-generated commit subjects verbatim.
- After a release, rename the `## [Unreleased]` content to `## [x.y.z] -
  YYYY-MM-DD`.

## [Unreleased]

### Added

- Separate docs repo per project (stealth mode): a project can keep ALL KainBain information (task docs, plans, reports, and the `.kainbain/` state incl. `project.json`) in a private git repo instead of the main repo, which then stays completely free of KainBain traces. Offered under an Advanced disclosure on project create/import and in Project Settings → Files & Repositories; stored redacted, one docs repo per project (409 on re-claim); runners check the docs repo out adjacent to the main repo with synced `kb/<taskId>` branches and push docs first at stage handoff (task 7f6220c3).

- System Settings gains an About tab (also at `#/system-settings/about`) showing the running UI, backend, and screen-to-server API versions with per-row update guides, a warning banner when a newer release is advertised, and the latest security report summary with a full-report link — all served by the new `GET /status/versions` endpoint. The API row ties the UI-reported contract (`frontend/version.json`) to the backend contract (`api/version.json`) with a compatibility verdict (the same API major stays compatible across asymmetric redeploys, with an alert on mismatch); unadvertised latest-release knobs (`KAINBAIN_LATEST_*_VERSION`) report Up to date, while a missing security report file (`KAINBAIN_SECURITY_REPORT_PATH`) still shows the honest "no security report recorded" state (task c5c465c4).

- Task goals render ` ```mermaid ` fences as inline SVG diagrams in the markdown viewer (mermaid lazy-loads only when a diagram is present and sanitizes at `strict` security level; a broken or unrenderable diagram degrades to its readable source block, never a blank hole), and the `creating-new-tickets` skill now drafts each ticket as its own markdown file under the task directory's `drafts/` folder before POSTing the file's exact contents, so API-created tickets land as structured documents (headings, steps, code, diagrams, image refs) instead of paragraphs; the first-line title, `blockedBy` validation, idempotency, and dedupe behave exactly as before (task 5a38ad45).

- Stage+config attestation for compliance proof: every per-stage wrap-up commit and its stage-history entry now carry the same task+stage config hash (git trailers plus a durable prose token with the commit SHA), verifiable offline with `node scripts/verify-stage-attestation.mjs --repo <path> --task <id>` (see the Stage Attestation site-docs article); clean-tree stages attest with an explicit null commit, and entries predating the feature stay valid without hashes (task d20f0c83).

===CHANGELOG===
# Changelog

All notable changes to KainBain are recorded here in **curated** form. The
per-commit baked history that backs the in-app **Changelog** dialog is generated
by `scripts/generate-changelog.mjs` and served through `GET /deploy/changelog`
(`frontend/src/components/layout/ChangelogModal.jsx`); it remains the exhaustive
source of truth. This file intentionally lists only high-impact changes.

## Update discipline

- Entries are curated **only at release time**, from the `Unreleased` section
  below, when a version tag/deploy is cut. Ordinary PRs are not required to touch
  this file (WP-10, task `8e61e197-cf8a-475e-b330-8cd7fa5a7e30`).
- Keep entries to one line each, grouped under `Added` / `Changed` / `Fixed` /
  `Removed` / `Security`. Reference the PR or task id in parentheses when
  helpful. Do not copy auto-generated commit subjects verbatim.
- After a release, rename the `## [Unreleased]` content to `## [x.y.z] -
  YYYY-MM-DD`.

## [Unreleased]

### Added

- Separate docs repo per project (stealth mode): a project can keep ALL KainBain information (task docs, plans, reports, and the `.kainbain/` state incl. `project.json`) in a private git repo instead of the main repo, which then stays completely free of KainBain traces. Offered under an Advanced disclosure on project create/import and in Project Settings → Files & Repositories; stored redacted, one docs repo per project (409 on re-claim); runners check the docs repo out adjacent to the main repo with synced `kb/<taskId>` branches and push docs first at stage handoff (task 7f6220c3).

- System Settings gains an About tab (also at `#/system-settings/about`) showing the running UI, backend, and screen-to-server API versions with per-row update guides, a warning banner when a newer release is advertised, and the latest security report summary with a full-report link — all served by the new `GET /status/versions` endpoint. The API row ties the UI-reported contract (`frontend/version.json`) to the backend contract (`api/version.json`) with a compatibility verdict (the same API major stays compatible across asymmetric redeploys, with an alert on mismatch); unadvertised latest-release knobs (`KAINBAIN_LATEST_*_VERSION`) report Up to date, while a missing security report file (`KAINBAIN_SECURITY_REPORT_PATH`) still shows the honest "no security report recorded" state (task c5c465c4).

- Task goals render ` ```mermaid ` fences as inline SVG diagrams in the markdown viewer (mermaid lazy-loads only when a diagram is present and sanitizes at `strict` security level; a broken or unrenderable diagram degrades to its readable source block, never a blank hole), and the `creating-new-tickets` skill now drafts each ticket as its own markdown file under the task directory's `drafts/` folder before POSTing the file's exact contents, so API-created tickets land as structured documents (headings, steps, code, diagrams, image refs) instead of paragraphs; the first-line title, `blockedBy` validation, idempotency, and dedupe behave exactly as before (task 5a38ad45).

- Stage+config attestation for compliance proof: every per-stage wrap-up commit and its stage-history entry now carry the same task+stage config hash (git trailers plus a durable prose token with the commit SHA), verifiable offline with `node scripts/verify-stage-attestation.mjs --repo <path> --task <id>` (see the Stage Attestation site-docs article); clean-tree stages attest with an explicit null commit, and entries predating the feature stay valid without hashes (task d20f0c83).

1|# Stage review — alias full-width follow-up (PR-review stage)
2|
3|Date: 2026-11-20. Scope: branch `kb/158394ab-3b43-4813-b94a-32d772a79972` vs `main`
4|(two commits: full-width section root, reasoning-test fix, kept-model wrap).
5|Method: guilty-until-proven-working — read the full diff, re-ran the repo's own
6|tests and gates, audited the width chain from app shell to chips, and inspected
7|the after-screenshots pixel-by-pixel. No servers started; nothing outside
8|`./docs` modified.
9|
10|## Verdict inputs
11|
12|- Goal achieved: YES. Section root is now `w-full min-w-0` (was `max-w-4xl` on
13|  `main`, `max-w-2xl` originally). Parent chain audited with no cap anywhere on
14|  the alias path: `App.jsx` main (`flex-1`, no max-w) → settings `section`
15|  (`flex-1`, no max-w) → tabpanel div (no class) → form wrapper
16|  (`border-t ...`, no max-w) → alias section (`w-full min-w-0`). The only
17|  `max-w-2xl` in `ProjectSettings.jsx:259` sits inside the `project`-tab-only
18|  conditional, so it cannot squeeze the aliases tab. Human correction ("make
19|  the most of the full width") is satisfied and locked by test.
20|- Plan followed: YES with one documented, human-directed deviation — plan Step 2
21|  defaulted to `max-w-4xl`, but the human rejection demanded full width and
22|  `DESIGN-NOTE.md` records the no-cap decision with rationale. Steps 0–1 and
23|  3–7 otherwise followed (seams, redesign, contract-test rewrite, screenshots,
24|  docs/a11y assessment).
25|- Standards: YES — `lint:frontend` 0 errors (alias files individually clean),
26|  `check:jsdoc-example` PASS, `check:one-function` PASS,
27|  `check:deps:frontend` PASS, duplicate-settings PASS. New modules keep
28|  `MARK:` + `@description` + runnable `@example` JSDoc.
29|- Modifiability: YES — one-function-per-file seams (`splitModelRefProvider`,
30|  `aliasTargetSummary`, `AliasTargetChip`, `AliasCollapsedRow`), shared grammar
31|  reuse (`parseModelKey`/`splitReasoning`), pure helpers with unit tests.
32|- Best practices: YES — full stored ref in DOM + sr-only (not title-only),
33|  fail-safe props, historic test ids preserved, frontend-only change.
34|- Tech debt: NONE added. The prior review's nit (reasoning-suffix test passing
35|  via sr-only text on a 3-segment ref) is fixed: 4-segment ref asserting the
36|  muted `::high` span plus a negative 3-segment case. Kept-model note edge case
37|  (`none` harness) now wraps via `break-all`, locked by a new overflow test.
38|- Docs: N/A correctly — no `site-docs/` page describes the collapsed layout
39|  (faq/agent-execution/submit-track-task mentions stay accurate), CHANGELOG
40|  convention says ordinary PRs must NOT touch it, in-app copy still matches.
41|  `check-doc-links` PASS (75 files).
42|
43|## Test evidence (observed in this session)
44|
45|- Focused: `npm run test:frontend -- ModelAliasesSection SettingsCards.overflow
46|  AliasCollapsedRow AliasTargetChip aliasTargetSummary splitModelRefProvider
47|  TruncatedText useCollapsibleRows` → 9 files, 173 tests, all pass.
48|- Full: `npm run test:frontend` → 362 files, 4936 tests, all pass, exit 0.
49|- `truncate` audit: the only remaining `truncate` on the alias screen is the
50|  alias *name* in the collapsed header (short by design, full text in `title`);
51|  no model ref is ellipsized.
52|- Not re-run: `npm run test:api` and the api-vitest leg of `npm run docs:check`
53|  (`api/node_modules` absent in this environment — pre-existing gap, unrelated
54|  to this frontend-only change; the doc-links and jsdoc legs pass standalone).
55|
56|## Visual evidence (inspected in this session)
57|
58|- `assets/alias-desktop-fullwidth.png` (PNG magic `89504e47` verified,
59|  1440x900): section spans the full panel; `gemini-3-pro-preview`,
60|  `claude-sonnet-4-5`, and a very long `quarterly-release-router-mmm…` ref all
61|  fully visible next to provider badges; error badge on its own readable line.
62|- `assets/alias-mobile-fullwidth.png` (390x853): chips stack full-width under
63|  the header, the long ref wraps inside its chip, error badge wraps — no
64|  clipping, no page overflow.
65|- Note: captures are mock-harness renders of the real components with repo
66|  tailwind (same method as the prior accepted review), corroborated by the new
67|  class assertions and the parent-chain audit above.

2|
3|Decision for the alias-screen redo (issue: model names cut off mid-name in the
4|collapsed summary, `assets/image.png`). Survey round-1 answers are still empty,
5|so the proposed defaults in `IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` §1 bind: q1 whole alias
6|screen, q2 wrap-before-ellipsis, q3 provider as a badge, q4 mobile gets its own
7|full-width line, q5 compact rows by default, q6 error badge on its own line.
8|
9|## Before (current markup, `ModelAliasesSection.jsx` ~:1238)
10|
11|```
12|┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
13|│ ▸ name │ summary-badge (one hard-truncated line) │ ⚠err │ rel │ ✕ │  ← one flex line, everything competes
14|└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
15|section root capped at max-w-2xl (672px) even on a 1440px+ desktop page
16|```
17|
18|`TruncatedText` applies `truncate` (one-line ellipsis), so a long
19|`provider::model` ref — exactly what the summary badge holds — is cut mid-name.
20|
21|## After (chosen layout)
22|
23|```
24|┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
25|│ ▸ name  reliability-line                              ✕        │  ← header line
26|│ ┌────────────────────────────┐ ┌────────────────────────────┐ │  ← line 2: full-width wrapping chips
27|│ │ 50% Muse [google] gemini-… │ │ 50% pi [anthropic] claude-…│ │    (data-testid=model-alias-summary-{i})
28|│ └────────────────────────────┘ └────────────────────────────┘ │
29|│ [⚠ error badge — own full-width line when present]            │
30|└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
31|section root spans the FULL width of the settings panel (no max-w cap) — this section only
32|```
33|
34|## Decisions
35|
36|- **(a) Two-line collapsed row.** Line 1 = toggle + alias name (still
37|  `truncate` — names are short by design) + reliability + delete. Line 2 =
38|  `w-full flex flex-wrap gap-1.5` chips container carrying
39|  `data-testid="model-alias-summary-{i}"` (existing test id survives on the
40|  container). On `<sm` the flex-wrap structure makes line 2 naturally
41|  full-width under the header (q4 option 1) — verified at 390px.
42|- **(b) Chip structure.** `percent` (bold, nowrap) + harness label (nowrap) +
43|  provider badge (small uppercase) + model id (`font-mono`, `min-w-0 flex-1`,
44|  `break-all` so it wraps before any ellipsis). Chip itself is
45|  `inline-flex flex-wrap` with `min-w-0`, so a 140+ char id wraps inside the
46|  chip instead of overflowing. Full stored ref (`harness::provider::id[::lvl]`)
47|  rides in the chip's `title` **and** an sr-only span inside the chip, so the
48|  complete ref is always in the DOM/accessibility tree (WCAG — hover alone is
49|  not enough).
50|- **(c) Truncation order.** chip wraps to next line → model id wraps
51|  (`break-all`) → single-line ellipsis only as last resort on the alias *name*
52|  (unchanged). Model refs are never ellipsized.
53|- **(d) Container width.** `max-w-2xl` → **no width cap at all** (`w-full
54|  min-w-0`) on the alias section root only, so the section uses the full width
55|  of the settings panel on desktop. Human review correction (final review

57|  1440px+ page — "make the most of the full width" means uncapped. Other
58|  settings tabs keep their `max-w-*` — intentional, noted in PR.
59|- **(e) Mobile.** No separate breakpoint needed: chips line is a full-width
60|  block under the header at every width; at 390px each chip takes the full row.
61|- **Provider split semantics** (`splitModelRefProvider`): strip optional
62|  `::reasoning` via `splitReasoning`, then split the base on the first `::`:
63|  - `google::gemini-3-pro` → `{ provider: 'google', modelId: 'gemini-3-pro' }`
64|  - `pi::google::m` (canonical 3-segment) → `{ provider: 'google', modelId: 'm' }`
65|    (the harness half is already shown by the harness label chip — not repeated)
66|  - bare `m` → `{ provider: '', modelId: 'm' }` (no badge rendered)
67|  - garbage/blank → `{ provider: '', modelId: ref }` (never throws)
68|

72|  verified `className` carries `w-full` and no `max-w-` class); all three
73|  chips (incl. a 204-char model id) render with `scrollWidth == clientWidth`
74|  — zero clipping; no horizontal page scroll.
75|- 390px: chips drop to full-width rows under the header; 204-char model id
76|  wraps inside its chip, fully contained, no page scroll.
77|

Read text file `docs/tasks/158394ab-3b43-4813-b94a-32d772a79972/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`.
1|# Implementation plan — Redo the Model Aliases screen so model names stop being cut off
2|
3|## 0. Goal
4|
5|The collapsed alias rows in Settings › Project Settings › Model Aliases truncate the model
6|summary to the point it is meaningless (screenshot: `assets/image.png`), even on desktop where
7|the rest of the page is empty. Model names carry provider prefixes (`google::gemini-3-pro`),
8|so a mid-name ellipsis destroys the information.
9|
10|Redo the alias UI so the full model reference is readable on desktop and mobile, while keeping
11|every existing behaviour intact: collapse/expand, weighted targets, validation errors, reliability
12|lines, delete, add, save/discard.
13|
14|In scope: the alias screen only — `frontend/src/components/settings/ModelAliasesSection.jsx`
15|(collapsed rows + expanded alias cards). Out of scope: the model picker on stage cards, any
16|backend/API change (none needed — this is a pure frontend layout/content change).
17|
18|Source request: task title + `assets/image.png`. Decision checklist: `SURVEY.md` (round 1,
19|questions q1–q6; answers not collected yet — see §1).
20|
21|## 1. Survey decision map (SURVEY.md round 1 — proposed defaults)
22|
23|The survey answers are still empty (`"answers": {}`), so each question gets a **proposed
24|default** derived from the issue text. Once answers land they are binding; if an answer
25|contradicts a default, only Step 0 (design spike) is revisited — Steps 1–4 are written to be
26|layout-agnostic.
27|
28|| # | Question | Proposed default (to bind when answered) |
29||---|---|---|
30|| q1 | Scope of the redo | The whole alias screen: collapsed summary rows **and** the expanded alias cards' headers. Not the stage-card model picker. |
31|| q2 | Overflow behaviour | Summary becomes its own wrapping area: model name gets the flexible width, wraps (`break-all`) before any ellipsis; small badges (reliability, warnings) sit on the first line with the name and never squeeze the model text. Ellipsis is the last resort, with the full ref always in `title` + the DOM. |
32|| q3 | Provider prefix | Model id renders as the main text with the provider as a small separate badge next to it (`google` badge + `gemini-3-pro`); the complete stored ref is never shortened in the DOM/accessibility tree — it stays in `title` and an sr-only span. |
33|| q4 | Mobile (narrow screen) | The model summary gets its own full-width line under the alias name (option 1), not a cut single line. |
34|| q5 | Many aliases | Keep compact collapsed rows by default (option 1) — one header line + one summary line per alias — full details on expand. No hover auto-expand. |
35|| q6 | Other pain points | Error/warning badges move to their own full-width line when present so they are never squeezed out; reliability line stays compact on the header line; percent split stays inside the expanded card. |
36|
37|## 2. Current-state map (verified in repo)
38|
39|Root causes of the cut-off names:
40|
41|1. **The section is width-capped.** `ModelAliasesSection.jsx:1148` renders
42|   `<div data-testid="model-aliases-section" className="space-y-3 max-w-2xl">` — 42rem (672px)
43|   max, while the settings page is much wider on desktop. This alone wastes the "rest of the
44|   page" the issue mentions. (Other settings tabs also use `max-w-2xl`, e.g.
45|   `ProjectSettings.jsx:259` — widening those is out of scope.)
46|2. **The collapsed row is one crowded flex line.** `ModelAliasesSection.jsx:1238` —
47|   `flex items-center justify-between gap-2 flex-wrap min-w-0` holds, in one row: the collapse
48|   toggle, the alias name (`truncate`, :1249), the summary badge (:1255–1260), the error badge
49|   (:1261+), the reliability line (:1283+), and the delete button (:1301+). Everything competes
50|   for the same width.
51|3. **The summary is a single hard-truncated string.** The badge wraps
52|   `<TruncatedText text={formatAliasSummary(targets, targetHarnesses)} />` (:1258).
53|   `TruncatedText` (`frontend/src/components/common/TruncatedText.jsx`) applies
54|   `min-w-0 max-w-full truncate inline-block` — a one-line ellipsis whose only full-text carrier
55|   is the hover `title`. `formatAliasSummary` (:854–880) builds one long string
56|   `"2 targets · 50% Muse (google::gemini-3-pro), 50% pi (…)"`, so a long provider-prefixed ref
57|   is exactly what gets cut.
58|4. **Model refs embed the provider.** Grammar in `shared/modelKeys.js` /
59|   `frontend/src/services/modelKeys.js`: canonical `harness::provider::id::reasoning`, legacy
60|   `provider::id`; `splitReasoning` (`shared/modelKeys.js:148`) splits the optional `::level`.
61|
62|Key files and contracts:
63|
64|| File | Role | Notes |
65||---|---|---|
66|| `frontend/src/components/settings/ModelAliasesSection.jsx` (1489 LOC) | The alias screen | MARK-documented sections: `formatAliasSummary` :854, `CollapseToggleButton` :882, `DeleteAliasButton` :914, `AliasTargetRow` :462, collapsed/expanded render :1238–1450 |
67|| `frontend/src/components/common/TruncatedText.jsx` + `.test.jsx` | Shared one-line truncation label | Used by all settings cards; keep unchanged for other cards |
68|| `frontend/src/components/settings/ReliabilityLine.jsx` | Per-alias / per-target reliability line | Rendered in the collapsed row today |
69|| `frontend/src/components/settings/useCollapsibleRows.js` + `.test.jsx` | Collapse state keyed by stable row keys | Not touched by this redo |
70|| `frontend/src/components/settings/ProjectSettingsForm.jsx:685–700` | Mount point (`activeFormSection === 'aliases'`) | Passes aliases/harnesses/fleetCounts/projectId |

74|
75|Stable test ids to preserve on the new markup: `model-aliases-section`, `model-alias-row`,
76|`model-alias-toggle-{i}`, `model-alias-summary-{i}`, `model-alias-error-alert-{i}` /
77|`model-alias-error-badge-{i}`, `alias-reliability-{i}`, `model-alias-body-{i}`.
78|
79|Repo rules that shape the implementation:
80|
81|- New files under `frontend/src/` are gated by `scripts/check-one-function-per-file.mjs`
82|  (one top-level function per new file) — so new pieces are **new files**, not more functions
83|  inside `ModelAliasesSection.jsx`.
84|- Every new/renamed export needs a `MARK:` + `@description` + runnable `@example` JSDoc block;
85|  gate: `npm run check:jsdoc-example` (see `docs/agent-docs/KB-Code-Standards.md` §Jsdoc).
86|- `npm run check:deps:frontend` guards declared imports.
87|- Accessibility: repo aligns to WCAG 2.2 AAA (`docs/accessibility/`); full model refs must stay
88|  in the DOM/accessibility tree — a hover tooltip alone is not enough.
89|
90|## 3. Approach — make the change easy, then make the change
91|
92|1. **Design spike first (Step 0)** — the only real unknown is the exact collapsed-row layout
93|   and truncation order. Settle it on a static mock before touching source.
94|2. **Make the change easy (Step 1)** — extract pure helpers + a presentational collapsed-row
95|   component into their own one-function-per-file modules with unit tests, while the current
96|   UI stays byte-identical and green. After this step the redo is prop-drilling, not surgery.
97|3. **Make the change (Steps 2–4)** — widen the container, swap the collapsed row to the new
98|   layout, polish the expanded header/error badge.
99|4. **Assure it (Steps 5–7)** — update/extend tests, headless screenshots at desktop + mobile
100|   widths, docs + accessibility pass. Full gates before merge.

109|  the full `harness::provider::id` ref in `title` + sr-only; (c) truncation order = chip wraps →
110|  model id wraps → ellipsis only as last resort; (d) container width: `max-w-2xl` → `max-w-4xl`

220|  markup.
221|- Add a `CHANGELOG.md` entry if the repo convention covers UI fixes (check existing entries).
222|- Gate: `npm run docs:check` green.

224|## 5. Ordering / dependencies
225|
226|`Step 0` → `Step 1` → `Step 2` → `Step 3` → `Step 4` → `Step 5` (tests updated alongside 3–4,
227|never after) → `Step 6` (screenshots) → `Step 7` (docs) → full gate `npm test -- --no-canary`
228|before merge. Steps 2–4 can ship in one PR once Step 1 lands; nothing backend-side is touched,
229|so api tests are regression-only.
230|
231|## 6. Acceptance table (from the survey; verify every row)
232|
233|| Survey | Expected behaviour | Verified by |
234||---|---|---|
235|| q1 | Redo covers collapsed rows + expanded alias cards; stage-card picker untouched | Step 3–4 diff scope; `ModelAliasesSection.test.jsx` |
236|| q2 | Long model names are readable at desktop width — chips wrap, model id wraps with `break-all`, ellipsis only as last resort with full ref in `title`/DOM | overflow test rewrite (Step 5) + 1440px screenshot |
237|| q3 | Provider shown as a small badge next to the model id; complete stored ref never shortened in DOM/a11y tree | `splitModelRefProvider` unit tests + chip component test + screenshot |
238|| q4 | At 390px the model summary is its own full-width line under the alias name | 390px screenshot + layout classes |
239|| q5 | Many aliases stay compact (one header line + one summary line each); expand shows details | `useCollapsibleRows.test.jsx` + collapse tests stay green |
240|| q6 | Error/warning badge on its own full-width line when present; reliability line compact on header | error-badge test + screenshot with an invalid row |

243|longer meaninglessly cut off on desktop** — shown by the 1440px after-screenshot.
244|
245|## 7. Assurance plan (how we prove it)
246|
247|- Unit/component: `npm run test:unit`; focused runs
248|  `npm run test:frontend -- ModelAliasesSection SettingsCards.overflow TruncatedText useCollapsibleRows`.
249|- Pre-push gates (all <1 min): `npm run lint:frontend`, `npm run check:jsdoc-example`,
250|  `npm run check:one-function`, `npm run check:deps:frontend`, `npm run docs:check`.
251|- Visual: `npm run capture:screenshot` at `--width 1440` and `--width 390` (headless, no
252|  background server); PNG magic self-verified by the script; before/after stored in
253|  `docs/tasks/158394ab-3b43-4813-b94a-32d772a79972/assets/`.
254|- Full gate before merge: `npm test -- --no-canary` (api untouched, so regression-only there).
255|- Manual checklist: real project with long `provider::model` refs → desktop + mobile viewport;
256|  keyboard-only expand/collapse (aria-expanded already asserted in tests); save/discard round-trip
257|  still submits collapsed rows (covered by existing transfer-safety tests).
258|- Docs: `site-docs/` settings page + in-app copy + CHANGELOG entry reviewed in the same PR;
259|  accessibility checklist (wcag-audit skill) run over the new collapsed-row markup.
260|
261|## 8. Risks
262|
263|- **Overflow-contract test churn**: `SettingsCards.overflow.test.jsx` deliberately changes meaning
264|  in Step 5 (truncate → readable-wrap). Other settings cards keep `TruncatedText` unchanged, so
265|  their tests stay green.
266|- **Section-width divergence**: only the aliases section leaves `max-w-2xl`; other tabs keep it.
267|  Intentional per the issue; a global settings-page widening is a separate task (note in PR).
268|- **jsdom cannot measure real layout**: wrap/truncation behaviour is proven by screenshots
269|  (Step 6), not by class assertions alone; class assertions are a secondary signal.
270|- **Survey answers pending**: §1 defaults stand in; if answers contradict, only Step 0's layout
271|  constants change — the Step 1 seams (helpers + presentational row) are layout-agnostic.
272|- **Very long unbroken model ids** (140+ chars): `break-all` on the chip's model text + full ref
273|  in `title`/sr-only keeps them contained without mid-name ellipsis; the chip itself may span
274|  multiple lines, which q2's wrap option explicitly allows.
275|- **Test-id drift**: any renamed test id breaks existing suites — §2 lists the ids that must
276|  survive; Step 5 updates only the summary-content assertions.

TITLE: Teach the Plan stage the RiskRegister template before Risk review

{"content":"# Retrospective — alias screen redo (task 158394ab)

Date: 2026-11-21. Stage: retrospective (docs-only). Author: agent.

## Ticket history

The alias screen truncated provider-prefixed model names mid-name while most
of the desktop page sat empty. The pipeline ran: survey (round 1, answers never
collected — plan proceeded on proposed defaults) → plan (IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md)
→ implementation (two-line collapsed rows, per-target chips) → PR review
(review-alias-redo: accepted at `max-w-4xl`/896px) → human rejection
("make the most of the full width") → full-width rework (`w-full min-w-0`,
reasoning-test fix, kept-model wrap) → second PR review (accepted).

## Structural pain points found

1. **Guessed width target, no measurable criterion.** The issue said the rest of
   the page was empty, yet the plan baked in `max-w-4xl` (896px of 1440px) and
   both agent stages accepted it. Only the human caught it, forcing a full
   rework loop. The surviving regression test
   (`SettingsCards.overflow.test.jsx`, "spans the full width") locks the section
   root/row classes but not the ancestor chain (`App.jsx` → settings section →
   tabpanel → `ProjectSettingsForm` wrapper → section), so a cap reintroduced
   on any ancestor (cf. `ProjectSettings.jsx:259` `max-w-2xl`) would silently
   re-squeeze the Aliases tab.
2. **Model-ref grammar trap produced a silently-wrong test.** `splitReasoning`
   (`shared/modelKeys.js:137-166`) returns a reasoning level only for 4-segment
   refs; the agent's chip test used 3-segment `google::m1::high` and passed via
   sr-only text instead of the muted-suffix span. Caught only in review; cost a
   second fix commit. No canonical ref fixtures exist anywhere in the repo.
3. **No reusable component-level visual-proof harness.** `capture-screenshot.mjs`
   needs a running app URL; clipping assertions exist only as one-off snippets
   (`mobile-responsive.spec.js`, `LogViewer.test.jsx`). The implementer skipped
   the required Step 6 screenshots, and the reviewer hand-rolled a scratch vite
   server (the forbidden ad-hoc-server pattern) to measure per-chip
   `scrollWidth` vs `clientWidth`.

Not ticketed (already covered): empty-survey scope drift (completed task
73f23a38), screenshot output path (completed b3ab7335), task-asset
materialization (completed b31cab50), feedback-asset validation (open 64fb8fbb).

## Dedupe

Resolved project `0fd41821…` (kainbain) → workflow `wf-default` → stage `1`
(Idea). Listed all 63 workflow tasks; none of the 11 non-completed tasks covers
these three findings (titles/goals inspected). Note: the skill's API base
`http://localhost:3100` refused connection on this runner; the reachable
backend from the runner env (`KAINBAIN_RUNNER_BACKEND`) is
`http://192.168.1.206:3100`, which was used instead.

## Tickets created (all `execute:false`, stage `1`/Idea, verified via re-read)

- `368363b6-2508-4ff7-ac83-3796f9394d52` — Lock the alias full-width contract
  across the whole render path (render-path no-cap test + measurable-criterion
  rule for Plan agents).
- `c2569064-b908-46c4-b69e-fe85bf1cc823` — Add canonical model-ref test fixtures
  so invented refs cannot silently pass (fixture module + grammar-trap doc).
- `ded73656-bda8-468c-b0be-396570e4d2d4` — Provide a reusable fixture-driven
  component clipping harness for visual proof (one-command no-clipping proof,
  no ad-hoc servers).

Each ticket goal stands alone and cites this task (`158394ab-3b43-4813-b94a-32d772a79972`)
plus the exact task-doc files as the case study. Current executing stage
(`stage-1794594754686`/retrospective) was never targeted.
